title: Westlife Foodworld Ltd - 505533 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q4 FY26 same-store sales grew 1.5% on mid-single-digit guest count growth; revenue up 9% to INR 6.6 billion.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 6.6 billion and same-store sales grew 1.5%, driven by mid-single-digit guest count growth, with positive footfall in all three months and momentum continuing into April. Full-year revenue grew 5% to INR 26.3 billion. Gross margin held near historic highs at 68.1% (up about 60 bps QoQ), and full-year cash PAT was INR 2.4 billion (9% of sales). Management said it is too early to call a sustained revival, and it guided to 60+ restaurant openings in FY27 versus a record 48 in FY26.

financial_highlights.change: About +60 bps QoQ; near historic highs

segments.name: West region
segments.commentary: Management described West as the strongest growth driver, though it was affected by LPG disruptions; no specific West SSS figure was given.

segments.name: South region
segments.commentary: Same-store sales ended the quarter nearly flat, a meaningful improvement on prior quarters, with guest count turning marginally positive after the company rolled back to everyday value (except Chennai, where it is a trial).

segments.name: Digital and delivery (McDelivery, app)
segments.commentary: Cumulative app downloads crossed 52 million with about 3.5 million monthly active users growing at double-digit YoY; delivery grew about 6% vs dine-in about 9%.

guidance_outlook: Open 60+ restaurants annually going forward (FY27), with all new stores fully digital-equipped and including McCafés; Vision 2027 target of 580-630 restaurants retained.
Gross margin in the near term indicated at around 67% or higher, reflecting current inflation partly offset by cost optimisation.
Price increases of 2-4% a year are the policy, but none taken in the last four to five months and no immediate plan; some small increases possible.

Vision 2027 target: first reach about INR 3,000 crore in sales; Ind AS EBITDA margin improvement to 13-15% expected mainly from operating leverage, with a breakup for the next two years to be given closer to FY27 start.
Aim to lift SSSG towards mid-single digits as early as possible.
Toys for Happy Meals expected to take about 9 to 12 months to return; books being used meanwhile.
Store closures of about 6-7 a year expected as part of portfolio management.
capex_capacity: Opened a record 48 restaurants in FY26, with 21 in Q4, taking the total to 478 restaurants across 78 cities.
Plan to open 60+ restaurants annually; partnerships with HPCL, BPCL and Jio-bp to expand highway footprint, plus airports, malls and six key metros.
Store closures in FY26 were about 6-7, attributed to malls shutting, highway access changes and lease tenure; management said this is not South-specific.
Store modernisation investment helped resilience: all restaurants operational, with fewer than 10% on limited menu due to LPG shortages.
demand_pricing: Q4 SSSG of 1.5% came with mid-single-digit guest count growth; management said it would not break out the Navratri and LPG effects, and that around 10% of stores were hit by LPG shortages from 10 March.
Growth is being driven by the 99 everyday value meal, with McCafé subscription (10 coffees a month for INR 55) and merchandise campaigns (sipper, tote bag) aimed at Gen Z.
Commodity pressure: cocoa and coffee inflation in FY26, offset by supply chain efficiencies and contract timing; management said last year's inflation tailwind may not repeat.
Management said it would hold product-mix margin dilution where it is and is not planning further value price cuts beyond current levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised SSG for Q4 after Navratri timing and supply disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to adjust further and said 1.5% SSSG is the number, with mid-single-digit guest count growth; momentum of 8-10% growth is seen in recent weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gross margin expanding and what is FY27 pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply chain initiatives and an internal cost project offset inflation; FY26 inflation was a tailwind that may not repeat. Pricing policy is 2-4% a year, but no price increase has been taken for four to five months and none is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why is store opening guidance 60+ versus the usual 40-50, and why the closures?
qa_highlights.answer: The 60+ number reflects Vision 2027 (580-630 restaurants) and penetration headroom; closures are portfolio management of about 6-7 a year and were not South-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Will the expansion target hold if the LPG and raw material pressure persists for six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident the store target holds, citing cost levers and industry-wide price increases as options if inflation rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the health and protein-led consumer read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mid-single-digit guest count growth shows no health-driven issue; it cited the Aloo Tikki balanced meal, lower sodium fries, reduced mayo fat, protein slice and millet bun as menu choices.

risks_watch: LPG shortages and geopolitical-driven commodity inflation (cocoa, coffee, supplier costs) could pressure gross margin below the 67% indication.
Delivery growth (about 6%) lags dine-in (about 9%); management wants equal growth from both channels.
Toy supply for Happy Meals still blocked by the BIS issue for about 9-12 months.
Store closures expected at 6-7 a year; whether the FY27 60+ opening pace is achieved.
SSSG remains only 1.5%, well below the mid-single-digit target; management would not call it a sustained revival.
summary.management_tone: Cautious-to-confident: management stressed that the revival is early and that the company will not call it sustained until more quarters show consistent momentum. Management was evasive on the sub-components of SSSG, on the Navratri effect and on the opex bps question, which it deferred offline.
key_quotes: Despite the challenges, we delivered a steady performance underpinned by improving guest count trends and sustained profitability.
we would refrain from calling this a sustained revival until we see a few more quarters and months of consistent momentum.
Value is not difficult in a current environment to get, but we wanted to really, really focus on volume.

adds.what: 60+ restaurant openings per year in FY27 (incl. McCafés, highway fuel-station partnerships with HPCL, BPCL, Jio-bp, airports, malls, six key metros)

growth.why: Management guides to 60+ restaurant openings in FY27 (vs record 48 in FY26) backed by named fuel-retail, airport, mall and metro partnerships, and says SSSG aim is mid-single digits, but gives no specific capex or timing beyond 'annually' and states it is too early to call a sustained revival; the 2-4% price policy is not being applied currently.
